```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
```

# Purpose

The thesis text claims a direction reversal: with only a store's own sales
history (Stage 5, condition 1), Auto-ARIMA beats XGBoost and LightGBM; with
the full calendar/store/promotion feature set (Stage 1), the boosted models
beat Auto-ARIMA by a wide margin. Every other significance claim in the
thesis (Section "Statistical Significance of the Main Comparisons") is backed
by a Diebold--Mariano test, but this specific claim, tree vs statistical
benchmark, in each information regime, was never tested. This file closes
that gap.

**Why a new file instead of extending an existing one.** `rossmann_stage5.Rmd`
does not retain per-observation predictions (only summary RMSE/MAPE), and it
does not fit Auto-ARIMA at all — its own comment says "for the Auto-ARIMA
comparison, use the ARIMA RMSE from the Stage 1 output," which is a *point
estimate* comparison, not a test. `rossmann_final_comprehensive.Rmd` fits
Auto-ARIMA (function `run_statistical_benchmarks`) but on the Stage 1
feature/date alignment, not Stage 5's origin-safe, lag84-trimmed sample. A
valid paired test needs identical (Store, Date) pairs across every model
being compared, so this file re-derives that intersection explicitly rather
than assuming the two pipelines line up.

**Caching.** `xgb-lgb-stage1`, `xgb-lgb-stage5`, and `arima` are the three
expensive chunks (model training, ~1115-store Auto-ARIMA) and are all cached.
After the first successful knit, editing anything in Sections 5 onward
(alignment, the DM tests, the print statements) re-knits in seconds, because
those downstream chunks are cheap and the expensive ones are read from
`rossmann_stage7_tree_vs_statistical_cache/` instead of recomputing. If you
change any code *inside* a cached chunk, only that chunk (and anything after
it) reruns; unrelated earlier cached chunks are untouched.

# 1. Packages and shared setup

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse); library(lubridate); library(zoo)
library(xgboost); library(lightgbm); library(forecast)
TRAIN_CSV <- "train.csv"; STORE_CSV <- "store.csv"
N_THREADS <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)
TEST_DAYS <- 42; VAL_FRAC <- 0.15; SEED <- 42; set.seed(SEED)

train_raw <- read_csv(TRAIN_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))
store_raw <- read_csv(STORE_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# 2. Stage 1 (full-feature) predictions, retained per observation

Rebuilds the Stage 1 feature matrix and refits XGBoost/LightGBM exactly as in
`rossmann_stage6.Rmd`, but keeps the row-level predictions with `Store` and
`Date` so they can be joined against Auto-ARIMA later.

```{r stage1-prep}
df1 <- train_raw %>% filter(Open == 1, Sales > 0) %>% left_join(store_raw, by = "Store") %>%
  mutate(Year = year(Date), Month = month(Date), Week = isoweek(Date), DayOfMonth = mday(Date),
         Quarter = quarter(Date), IsWeekend = as.integer(DayOfWeek %in% c(6, 7)),
         StateHoliday = case_when(StateHoliday == "a" ~ 1L, StateHoliday == "b" ~ 2L,
                                  StateHoliday == "c" ~ 3L, TRUE ~ 0L),
         CompetitionOpenMonths = ifelse(!is.na(CompetitionOpenSinceYear) & !is.na(CompetitionOpenSinceMonth),
           (Year - CompetitionOpenSinceYear) * 12 + (Month - CompetitionOpenSinceMonth), NA_real_),
         CompetitionOpenMonths = pmax(CompetitionOpenMonths, 0, na.rm = TRUE),
         StoreType = as.integer(factor(StoreType, levels = c("a", "b", "c", "d"))),
         Assortment = as.integer(factor(Assortment, levels = c("a", "b", "c")))) %>%
  select(Store, Date, Sales, DayOfWeek, Promo, StateHoliday, SchoolHoliday, StoreType, Assortment,
         CompetitionDistance, Promo2, Year, Month, Week, DayOfMonth, Quarter, IsWeekend, CompetitionOpenMonths)
med1 <- median(df1$CompetitionDistance, na.rm = TRUE)
df1 <- df1 %>% mutate(CompetitionDistance = replace_na(CompetitionDistance, med1),
                      CompetitionOpenMonths = replace_na(CompetitionOpenMonths, 0)) %>%
  arrange(Date, Store)

FEAT_S1 <- c("Store", "DayOfWeek", "Promo", "StateHoliday", "SchoolHoliday", "StoreType", "Assortment",
  "CompetitionDistance", "Promo2", "Year", "Month", "Week", "DayOfMonth", "Quarter", "IsWeekend",
  "CompetitionOpenMonths")

split_data <- function(data, fc, td = TEST_DAYS) {
  data <- data %>% arrange(Date, Store); d <- sort(unique(data$Date)); cut <- d[length(d) - td]
  tr <- data %>% filter(Date <= cut); te <- data %>% filter(Date > cut)
  list(X_train = as.matrix(tr[, fc]), y_train = tr$Sales, X_test = as.matrix(te[, fc]),
       y_test = te$Sales, train = tr, test = te)
}
val_idx <- function(tr, vf = VAL_FRAC) { d <- sort(unique(tr$Date)); which(tr$Date > d[floor(length(d) * (1 - vf))]) }

fit_xgb <- function(sp) {
  X <- sp$X_train; y <- sp$y_train; vi <- val_idx(sp$train); ti <- setdiff(seq_along(y), vi)
  pr <- list(objective = "reg:squarederror", eta = 0.10, max_depth = 6, subsample = 0.8,
             colsample_bytree = 0.8, nthread = N_THREADS, verbosity = 0)
  e <- xgb.train(pr, xgb.DMatrix(X[ti, ], label = y[ti]), nrounds = 1500,
                 watchlist = list(val = xgb.DMatrix(X[vi, ], label = y[vi])),
                 early_stopping_rounds = 50, verbose = 0)
  f <- xgb.train(pr, xgb.DMatrix(X, label = y), nrounds = e$best_iteration, verbose = 0)
  predict(f, xgb.DMatrix(sp$X_test))
}
fit_lgb <- function(sp) {
  X <- sp$X_train; y <- sp$y_train; vi <- val_idx(sp$train); ti <- setdiff(seq_along(y), vi)
  pr <- list(objective = "regression", metric = "rmse", num_leaves = 63, learning_rate = 0.05,
             bagging_fraction = 0.8, bagging_freq = 1, feature_fraction = 0.8,
             num_threads = N_THREADS, seed = SEED, verbosity = -1)
  e <- lgb.train(pr, lgb.Dataset(X[ti, ], label = y[ti]), nrounds = 2000,
                 valids = list(val = lgb.Dataset(X[vi, ], label = y[vi])),
                 early_stopping_rounds = 50, verbose = -1)
  f <- lgb.train(pr, lgb.Dataset(X, label = y), nrounds = e$best_iter, verbose = -1)
  predict(f, sp$X_test)
}
```

```{r xgb-lgb-stage1, cache=TRUE}
sp1 <- split_data(df1, FEAT_S1)
pred_stage1 <- sp1$test %>%
  transmute(Store, Date, Sales,
            XGBoost = fit_xgb(sp1),
            LightGBM = fit_lgb(sp1))
```

# 3. Stage 5, condition 1 (history only) predictions, retained per observation

Same origin-safe lag construction as `rossmann_stage5.Rmd`; the only change is
that predictions are kept at the row level instead of collapsed to RMSE.

```{r stage5-prep}
df0 <- train_raw %>% filter(Open == 1, Sales > 0) %>% left_join(store_raw, by = "Store") %>%
  mutate(Year = year(Date), Month = month(Date)) %>%
  select(Store, Date, Sales, Year, Month)
add_origin_safe <- function(s) {
  s <- s %>% arrange(Date)
  s$lag42 <- lag(s$Sales, 42); s$lag49 <- lag(s$Sales, 49)
  s$lag56 <- lag(s$Sales, 56); s$lag84 <- lag(s$Sales, 84)
  s$origin_roll7 <- lag(rollmeanr(s$Sales, 7, fill = NA), 42)
  s$origin_roll28 <- lag(rollmeanr(s$Sales, 28, fill = NA), 42)
  s
}
df5 <- df0 %>% group_by(Store) %>% group_modify(~ add_origin_safe(.x)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(lag84), !is.na(origin_roll28)) %>% arrange(Date, Store)
HISTORY <- c("Store", "lag42", "lag49", "lag56", "lag84", "origin_roll7", "origin_roll28")
```

```{r xgb-lgb-stage5, cache=TRUE}
sp5 <- split_data(df5, HISTORY)
pred_stage5 <- sp5$test %>%
  transmute(Store, Date, Sales,
            XGBoost = fit_xgb(sp5),
            LightGBM = fit_lgb(sp5))
```

# 4. Auto-ARIMA on the exact evaluation dates of both regimes

Auto-ARIMA needs only a store's own daily history, so one fit per store
covers both regimes; what differs is which (Store, Date) rows are scored
against it, fixed in Section 5 by an inner join.

```{r arima, cache=TRUE}
eval_stores <- sort(unique(union(pred_stage1$Store, pred_stage5$Store)))
test_start <- min(pred_stage1$Date, pred_stage5$Date)
test_end   <- max(pred_stage1$Date, pred_stage5$Date)
horizon    <- as.integer(test_end - (test_start - days(1)))

train_daily <- train_raw %>% left_join(store_raw, by = "Store") %>%
  filter(Store %in% eval_stores, Date < test_start) %>% select(Store, Date, Sales)

fit_arima_store <- function(store_id) {
  d <- train_daily %>% filter(Store == store_id) %>% arrange(Date)
  calendar <- tibble(Date = seq(min(d$Date), test_start - days(1), by = "day")) %>%
    left_join(d, by = "Date") %>% mutate(Sales = replace_na(Sales, 0))
  y <- ts(calendar$Sales, frequency = 7)
  pred <- tryCatch(
    as.numeric(forecast::forecast(
      forecast::auto.arima(y, seasonal = TRUE, stepwise = TRUE, approximation = TRUE,
                           max.p = 3, max.q = 3, max.P = 1, max.Q = 1, max.order = 5),
      h = horizon)$mean),
    error = function(e) rep(mean(y), horizon))
  tibble(Store = store_id, Date = seq(test_start, test_end, by = "day"), ARIMA = pmax(0, pred))
}
pred_arima <- map_dfr(eval_stores, fit_arima_store)
```

# 5. Aligning the three prediction sets and running the DM tests

Everything from here on is cheap (joins, aggregation, a handful of t-tests),
so re-knitting after changing only this section reuses the three cached
chunks above and finishes in seconds.

```{r align}
regime1 <- pred_stage1 %>% inner_join(pred_arima, by = c("Store", "Date"))
regime5 <- pred_stage5 %>% inner_join(pred_arima, by = c("Store", "Date"))
cat(sprintf("Full-feature (Stage 1) aligned rows: %d\nHistory-only (Stage 5) aligned rows: %d\n",
            nrow(regime1), nrow(regime5)))
cat(sprintf("Full-feature unique test dates: %d\nHistory-only unique test dates: %d\n",
            n_distinct(regime1$Date), n_distinct(regime5$Date)))
```

```{r dm-tests}
# Same construction as rossmann_stage6.Rmd's E2: daily-aggregated squared
# error series, dm.test on their square roots (power = 2 compares the
# original squared-error loss). H0: E[d_t] = 0 (equal expected loss).
daily_sq <- function(data, model_col) {
  data %>% mutate(sq = (Sales - .data[[model_col]])^2) %>%
    group_by(Date) %>% summarise(l = mean(sq), .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(Date) %>% pull(l)
}
dm_row <- function(l1, l2, lab) {
  dm <- dm.test(sqrt(l1), sqrt(l2), alternative = "two.sided", h = 1, power = 2)
  # NOTE: dm$parameter is NOT the test's degrees of freedom -- dm.test()
  # returns c(forecasthorizon = h, lossfunctionpower = power) there, i.e. the
  # h=1/power=2 settings we passed in. The DM statistic's actual reference
  # distribution is t with (n_days - 1) df; we compute that ourselves.
  tibble(Comparison = lab, n_days = length(l1), DM = unname(dm$statistic),
         df = length(l1) - 1, p = dm$p.value)
}

results_stage7 <- bind_rows(
  dm_row(daily_sq(regime1, "XGBoost"),  daily_sq(regime1, "ARIMA"),  "Full-feature: XGBoost vs Auto-ARIMA"),
  dm_row(daily_sq(regime1, "LightGBM"), daily_sq(regime1, "ARIMA"),  "Full-feature: LightGBM vs Auto-ARIMA"),
  dm_row(daily_sq(regime5, "XGBoost"),  daily_sq(regime5, "ARIMA"),  "History-only: XGBoost vs Auto-ARIMA"),
  dm_row(daily_sq(regime5, "LightGBM"), daily_sq(regime5, "ARIMA"),  "History-only: LightGBM vs Auto-ARIMA")
) %>% mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p, method = "holm"))

rmse_check <- bind_rows(
  regime1 %>% summarise(Regime = "Full-feature", XGBoost = sqrt(mean((Sales - XGBoost)^2)),
                        LightGBM = sqrt(mean((Sales - LightGBM)^2)), ARIMA = sqrt(mean((Sales - ARIMA)^2))),
  regime5 %>% summarise(Regime = "History-only", XGBoost = sqrt(mean((Sales - XGBoost)^2)),
                        LightGBM = sqrt(mean((Sales - LightGBM)^2)), ARIMA = sqrt(mean((Sales - ARIMA)^2)))
)

# Plain-text print (not the paged/DataTables widget): avoids any ambiguity in
# copying numbers out of the rendered HTML, and n_days/df are shown explicitly
# so the test's effective sample size is checkable at a glance.
print(as.data.frame(results_stage7), row.names = FALSE)
print(as.data.frame(rmse_check), row.names = FALSE)
```

A negative DM statistic means the first-named model (XGBoost or LightGBM) has
the lower loss; a positive statistic means Auto-ARIMA does. `n_days` is the
number of daily loss observations the test is run on (should be close to the
42-day holdout, minus any dates dropped by the inner join), and `df` is
`dm.test`'s reported degrees of freedom, `n_days - 1` for `h = 1`; if `df` is
much smaller than `n_days - 1`, that is a sign something upstream (most
likely a `Date` mismatch in the join) silently dropped observations and the
test should not be trusted before that is fixed. Read together with
`rmse_check`, this is the formal version of the thesis's qualitative claim:
it should show a significant XGBoost/LightGBM advantage in the full-feature
row and a significant Auto-ARIMA advantage in the history-only row, matching
Table stage5's point estimates (XGBoost 1843, LightGBM 1852, Auto-ARIMA 1508
on history-only; XGBoost 1003, LightGBM 1013, Auto-ARIMA 1508 on the full
feature set) but now with a $p$-value attached to each claim rather than just
an RMSE gap.

```{r save}
write_csv(results_stage7, "rossmann_outputs/tab_stage7_tree_vs_statistical.csv")
# Written for the thesis: Table 18 (Diebold-Mariano tests, trees against the
# statistical benchmarks).
dir.create("thesis_tables", showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(results_stage7, "thesis_tables/stage7_dm_tests.csv")
write_csv(rmse_check, "rossmann_outputs/tab_stage7_rmse_check.csv")
```
